message.content:
The first risk is that supply chain constraints govern Keysight's ability to convert demand into revenue over the next several quarters, with management describing the supply environment as less flexible than a year earlier and calling the supply chain the governor of near-term revenue [D3]. That risk would be confirmed by fourth quarter revenue falling below the guided range of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion [D1].

The second risk is that the one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 that management said will not repeat set a high comparison bar for future profitability [D3]. That risk would be confirmed by earnings per share falling below the guided range of $3.34 to $3.40 in a later quarter [D1].

The third risk is that growth is concentrated in the Communications Solutions Group, whose revenue rose 43.09 percent from a year earlier to $1.35 billion [D1]. That risk would be confirmed by Communications Solutions Group revenue falling below $1.35 billion in a later quarter [D1].

The fourth risk is that global economic conditions, tariff and trade policy impacts, export control regulations and customer purchasing decisions and timing could cause results to differ materially from expectations [D1]. That risk would be confirmed by revenue growth on a year earlier falling below 36.54 percent in a later quarter [D1].
